note: Search API Stats logs every non-empty-keyword Search API query into its own `search_api_stats` DB table via hook_search_api_results_alter(), and registers that table as a Views base table (hook_views_data) with a relationship to users. It has no settings form, no configure route, no Drush, no plugin types. Its only alter hook is hook_search_api_stats_record_alter() (the ->alter('search_api_stats_record', $fields) call before insert). The shipped default view is Drupal-7-era code that does NOT load on D11, so reporting means building your own View on the search_api_stats base table. All medium/hard cases are grounded in that real table/columns and the Views base table: introspection reads back seeded rows (a known result count / the top keyword by count); execution builds a View whose base_table is search_api_stats, and clears the log table.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with the search_api_stats module, how does a visitor's keyword search end up recorded, and where is it stored? Name the hook that triggers the recording and the database table rows are inserted into.
evals.expected_output: search_api_stats implements hook_search_api_results_alter(); after a Search API query with non-empty keywords, it inserts one row (server, index, keywords, numfound, uid, timestamp, language, ...) into the search_api_stats table.

evals.prompt: I enabled search_api_stats on Drupal 11 but I do not see any search report page. How am I supposed to view the recorded statistics, and why is there no ready-made report out of the box?
evals.expected_output: The module exposes the search_api_stats table as a Views base table (hook_views_data) so you build your own View on it (e.g. group by keywords for top terms). The bundled default view uses the Drupal 7 hook_views_default_views() API and does not load on Drupal 11, so there is no working out-of-the-box report.

evals.prompt: With search_api_stats, which hook lets another module modify the fields of a search-statistics row before it is written to the database (for example to hash the session id or drop a keyword)?
evals.expected_output: hook_search_api_stats_record_alter(array &$fields): the module calls \Drupal::moduleHandler()->alter('search_api_stats_record', $fields) just before the insert, so implementers can rewrite the s_name/i_name/keywords/uid/sid/etc. array.

evals.prompt: This site's search_api_stats log contains a recorded search for the exact keyword 'sasneedle_zorp'. Inspect the live database and tell me how many results (numfound) that recorded search returned.
evals.expected_output: 77 - the row in the search_api_stats table with keywords='sasneedle_zorp' has numfound=77.

evals.prompt: Using the search_api_stats log on this site, for the Search API index whose i_name is 'sas_topidx', which keyword has been searched the most times? Inspect the live search_api_stats table and give that keyword.
evals.expected_output: sasterm_alpha - grouping the search_api_stats rows where i_name='sas_topidx' by keywords and counting, sasterm_alpha appears 3 times vs sasterm_beta once.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal 11 site, search_api_stats records searches but ships no working report. Create a View with the machine id 'sas_report' whose base table is the module's search_api_stats table (so it can report on recorded searches). Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A views.view.sas_report config entity exists with base_table: search_api_stats (created via the Views UI choosing the 'Search API stats' base table, or by importing the config).

evals.prompt: For a data-retention cleanup, I need the recorded search statistics for the search server named 'sasclear' removed from this site. Delete those search_api_stats log entries from the live database.
evals.expected_output: No rows remain in the search_api_stats table with s_name='sasclear' (the module has no purge UI; delete directly, e.g. DELETE FROM search_api_stats WHERE s_name='sasclear').
